_readme: Generated from data/games/tested/*.json and data/games/untested/*.json by tools/build-known-games.sh; do not edit by hand. Field reference: data/schema.json and README.md, "Contributing to the known games database".

games.name: Aliens versus Predator Classic 2000
games.notes: Both stores label this 'Classic 2000' to set it apart from 2010's Aliens vs. Predator, an unrelated later game by a different developer.

games.name: Arx Fatalis
games.notes: On Linux, the Arx Libertatis engine reimplementation (arx-libertatis.org) is a strong alternative: it runs natively without Wine or Proton, reuses your existing Arx Fatalis data files, and reproduces the game's environmental reverb through OpenAL Soft's EFX out of the box. It's self-contained, so use it or this script's approach, not both.

games.name: Assassin's Creed
games.notes: The PC 'Director's Cut Edition' sold on both stores isn't a remaster — it's the original 2008 PC port of the 2007 console game, with four PC-exclusive bonus missions and DirectX 10 support added on top.

gog.store_details: The classic pre-2013 build, sold by GOG as a standalone product separate from 'Baldur's Gate II: Enhanced Edition'. GOG's catalogue search doesn't surface it, but the product page and existing owners' libraries resolve normally. This build has real DirectSound3D EAX, unlike the Enhanced Edition's OpenAL rewrite. Its EAX 2.0 environmental occlusion historically needed VxD drivers under Windows 9x (per the Vogons Wiki citation for this title), which is likely moot under Wine.

games.name: Baldur's Gate II: Enhanced Edition

eax.problem: The Enhanced Edition runs on a from-scratch OpenAL engine, built for its native Linux and macOS ports — it never had DirectSound3D EAX to begin with.

games.notes: If you also own the classic build, it's a separate GOG product the scanner detects on its own — see the 'Baldur's Gate 2 Complete' entry (gog_id 1207658893), which has real DirectSound3D EAX.

games.name: Deus Ex

audio_fixes.title: Enable EAX reverb
audio_fixes.reason: Deus Ex ships with its hardware sound option off, and it only plays EAX reverb with it on.

games.notes: Reverb is used sparingly and is quiet by default — Battery Park, the first mission, is a good place to hear it. The community ALAudio mod doesn't pass the game's EAX reverb through, so stay on the default Galaxy driver (per kcat/dsoal#79).

audio_fixes.title: Enable EAX effects
audio_fixes.reason: Quake 4 ships with its EAX sound options off, so there's no reverb and no muffling of sounds through walls.

audio_fixes.title: Enable 5.1 surround sound
audio_fixes.reason: Quake 4 mixes its sound for two speakers by default.

extra_fixes.title: Fix low-res textures
extra_fixes.reason: Quake 4 can't detect how much memory modern graphics cards have, so it loads its lowest-resolution textures (per PCGamingWiki).
extra_fixes.follow_up: Open Options -> Video and click Autodetect.

games.name: System Shock 2

steam.store_details: The classic 1999 build was delisted from Steam in October 2025; Steam now sells only the 25th Anniversary Remaster, a separate ground-up rewrite with no DirectSound3D EAX support.
steam.patches: The System Shock 2 Community Patch (SCP) is worth pairing, though it's general bugfix/polish, not audio-specific.

gog.store_details: The original 1999 build's own GOG listing was delisted in October 2025 — GOG now sells only the 25th Anniversary Remaster, a separate ground-up rewrite with no DirectSound3D EAX support — but existing owners of the classic build keep access.
gog.patches: The System Shock 2 Community Patch (SCP) is worth pairing, though it's general bugfix/polish, not audio-specific.

audio_fixes.title: Enable underwater reverb
audio_fixes.reason: Some System Shock 2 maps don't mark their underwater areas, so they play the wrong reverb there (per NewDark's documentation).

extra_fixes.title: Enable full-precision mouse look
extra_fixes.reason: System Shock 2 reads mouse look through standard Windows input by default, which doesn't give high-resolution mice their full precision (per NewDark's documentation).

games.notes: It comes with NewDark pre-installed, which has its own OpenAL Soft 'Hardware Acceleration' option in the in-game Audio menu — worth trying if EAX doesn't sound right.

games.name: System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster

eax.problem: The 25th Anniversary Remaster runs on Nightdive's proprietary Kex Engine, a from-scratch rewrite — it never had DirectSound3D EAX to begin with.

games.notes: If you own the classic 1999 build, run this script against that installation instead — it has real DirectSound3D EAX support (plus NewDark's own OpenAL Soft 'Hardware Acceleration' option), neither of which this remaster's rewritten engine provides.

games.name: Unreal Tournament: Game of the Year Edition

steam.store_details: Delisted from Steam in December 2022, when Epic pulled the entire classic Unreal series from sale. OldUnreal (oldunreal.com) distributes a free, Epic-authorized copy of the full game.
steam.patches: Creative's official 'EAX Library Patch' (uteaxsys.zip, then uteaxdm.zip and uteaxctf.zip) adds full EAX 2.0 reverb and occlusion to the original Deathmatch and Capture the Flag maps — historically mirrored at patches-scrolls.com; verify the mirror and files before installing. OldUnreal's own patches also add a selectable OpenAL-based 'ALAudio' renderer, a strong alternative if you'd rather use it than this script's approach.

audio_fixes.reason: Unreal Tournament ships with its hardware sound option off, and it only plays EAX reverb with it on.
